_comment: Every character the prologue script needs, in script order of appearance.
Derived from Hollow Crown - Prologue Gameplay Script, 'Beyond the Wall'.
This supersedes the earlier vertical_slice_characters.json, which was built
from brief section 69 before the script existed. Two differences matter:
the prologue boss is the WALLSTALKER, not a goblin commander, and the cast
includes Aldric, Varric, Tomas, Edrin and the refugees. See
IMPORTANT: named characters use text-to-3d here, which makes them
BLOCKOUTS. Brief section 55 requires approved front/side/back concept art
for anything named. Add the URLs to 'references' and regenerate; the
Palette assignments come from docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md. No two characters in the
same scene share an accent hue.

assets.subject: young human swordsman soldier in a light blue tabard over leather armour, short dark hair, a single asymmetric pauldron on the left shoulder, and a short travelling cape
assets.extra: cape and single pauldron carry the silhouette
assets.notes: Protagonist. Needs run and victory for the escape sequence and battle results. Blockout until concept art is approved.

assets.subject: young human apprentice mage in a deep violet robe with wide sleeves, a short shoulder cloak, long light hair tied back, holding a simple wooden staff
assets.extra: wide sleeves and staff carry the silhouette
assets.notes: Apprentice mage, not yet a full mage. Casts Spark in battle 01. Blockout until concept art is approved.

assets.subject: young human soldier in a Greenvale guard tabard over mail, cropped sandy hair, a round shield on the back and a long spear
assets.extra: spear length is the readable silhouette, deliberately taller than Rowan
assets.notes: Party member in both prologue battles. Stays in Greenvale at the end and returns later, so he needs a full animation set rather than an NPC's.

assets.subject: weathered human captain in his late forties, greying beard, a worn officer's surcoat over mail, a heavy sword at the hip, no helmet
assets.extra: grey beard and bare head separate him from every helmeted soldier
assets.notes: Mentor. Draws his sword on Varric in scene 09, so he needs attack_1 despite being an NPC. If he ever becomes recruitable, move him to the hero budget.

assets.subject: cold human officer in polished dark plate with a tall crested helm and a long crimson half-cloak, mounted officer's sword
assets.extra: polished and immaculate, deliberately the cleanest figure in a dusty scene
assets.notes: Antagonist of the prologue, not a villain. Fights alongside Rowan against the Wallstalker.

assets.subject: young human guard recruit in a plain Greenvale tabard over padded cloth, untidy hair, holding a training sword
assets.notes: Training yard only. Script flags him as memorable for a possible return when Rowan comes home.

assets.subject: human Greenvale soldier in a green tabard over mail with a conical helm, round shield and short sword
assets.extra: faceless by design so the mesh can be reused across the whole squad
assets.notes: Reused for the gate guard, the training yard guards, Captain Heron's unconscious men and Varric's squad in battle 02. One mesh, recoloured and rescaled per role.

assets.subject: stooped elderly human woman in a long brown shawl and apron, grey hair in a bun, holding a wicker basket
assets.notes: The mother hint in Greenvale. Needs no combat animations.

assets.subject: small human village child in a simple ochre tunic and bare feet, messy hair
assets.extra: roughly two thirds the height of an adult villager
assets.notes: Runs away after Maeve's giant joke, so it needs run.

assets.subject: broad human blacksmith in a heavy leather apron over bare arms, cloth head wrap, holding a hammer
assets.extra: widest villager silhouette, bare arms read at distance

assets.subject: gaunt human man in unfamiliar layered travelling clothes of teal and dusty ochre, a wrapped headscarf and a heavy pack
assets.extra: clothing must read as foreign against every Greenvale palette
assets.notes: Brief section 6 and the script both hang on this: the refugees must look like they come from somewhere the player has never seen. Their palette is outer_world, not greenvale, and that contrast is the story reveal.

assets.subject: human woman in unfamiliar layered travelling clothes of teal and dusty ochre, a long shawl, carrying a bundled infant
assets.notes: Maeve's line 'unless monsters have started carrying babies' depends on this silhouette being readable through a crack in the wall.

assets.subject: small human child in oversized unfamiliar travelling clothes of faded teal, clutching a cloth doll
older human man in unfamiliar layered clothing with a weathered leather coat, close-cropped grey hair and a long scar, carrying a battered sword
assets.extra: the coat and scar mark him out from the other refugees
assets.notes: Delivers the 'you think this wall protects you' beat. Likely recurring, so treat as a named character and get concept art.

assets.subject: small hunched goblin in mismatched scrap leather with a notched cleaver, oversized pointed ears and a broad grin
assets.extra: sickly green skin, rust-red faction rag, low crouched profile

assets.subject: small goblin in scrap leather with a crude long spear and a plank shield, rust-red arm wrap
assets.extra: same green and rust palette as the raider, spear makes the two-tile reach readable
assets.notes: Two in battle 01. One flees north toward the Wall in the mid-battle event, so it needs run.

assets.subject: small goblin archer with a crude short bow, a scrap-leather chest wrap and a rust-red headband
assets.extra: same green and rust palette as the raider
assets.notes: One in battle 01. Takes the hill to demonstrate height advantage.

assets.subject: alien armoured quadruped beast with a chitinous plated head shield, four long blade-tipped limbs and no visible eyes, void violet carapace with pale gold seams
assets.extra: heavily plated front, exposed soft flank and rear, silhouette unlike any known monster
assets.notes: Prologue mini-boss, level 3. Its armoured front and weak flanks are the positioning tutorial, so the plating must be visually obvious from the tactical camera or the mechanic is unfair. Palette is the sealed-fragment faction from the style guide, not the goblin faction: this is the player's first glimpse of what the Crownwall really holds.
